newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Two killed in gunbattle in S.Africa Zulu province.
newsitem.headline: Two killed in gunbattle in S.Africa Zulu province.

text.p: Two people were killed in gun battles between Zulu residents of a predominantly African National Congress area in South Africa's KwaZulu-Natal province, police said on Wednesday.
Police reported a 40-year-old man was shot dead in Fredville north of Durban on Tuesday night and a 25-year-old man was found dead after gunshots were heard in the area on Wednesday morning.
Soldiers have been sent into the area which was reported to be quiet but tense by Wednesday afternoon.
The fighting broke out during a gap left by troops stationed in the area being withdrawn and fresh troops being sent in, said Inkatha Freedom Party safety and security spokesman Philip Powell.
"Fighting broke out in the vacuum that was left by the soldiers being pulled out, but their replacements are back in force," Powell told Reuters.
He said a provincial parliamentary safety and security committee comprising members of the ANC and Inkatha had visited the area to probe the reasons for the violence.
"There was agreement between ANC and Inkatha members of parliament that policing in the area is inadequate and we have facilitated peace talks between all sides.
"It is a very complicated, murky situation and it seems to be a result of a longstanding conflict within the ANC," he said.
The ANC was not immediately available for comment.
Police said over 15 people have been killed in the area since last December, including six who were killed by gunmen in an attack on a homestead in December.
